lists.name: RYM Top — Rock — Garage Rock Revival
1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die

podcast.body: This album, their second full-length release, adhered to the band's five-syllable album title rule. It was initially released in the UK and then in North America in February 2005, roughly five months later. This staggered release was due to the band's early success in the UK, where they were associated with a "new rock revival" that included bands like The Strokes. The album yielded three major singles in the UK, all of which made the Top 20, including "The Bucket" and "King of the Rodeo". "This record got a British release first and an North American release second."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Kings of Leon in Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.body: This second album was largely influenced by the band's extensive touring in Europe and the UK between their first and second records, during which they experienced the "highs of rock and roll." The lyrical content explicitly reflected themes of excess, including boozing, drugging, and women. "AHA Shake, the second record, which was pretty much about boozing and drugging and women and all that good stuff."
